objective: Compose the existing TCS1-4 timing laws with checked profile-derived DCS1 depth, using the same committed water view and event owner.
design: Introduce an explicit profile-aware TCS1-4/DCS1 entry. Obtain deficit and AWLH/AWMH/AWAH in one checked aggregation. TCS1 retains supplied daily stress observations; TCS2-4 consume derived water aggregates. Pass derived deficit in a local request copy and typed timing selection to the shared scheduled process, retaining its DCS1 correction, rainfall reduction, clipping, rate and event equations. Do not allow the existing profile-free TCS1-4 entry to accept DCS1 accidentally. Pending and ineligible intervals bypass new aggregation and timing evaluation. Bootstrap wiring follows source gates and uses its existing snapshot only.
gates: Re-read DCS1 and timing source-oracle contracts before implementation; compare combined gift depth and duration against independent source equations for all four criteria.
Positive and zero clipped depth, correction interpolation, rainfall switch, timing false, fixed precedence and invalid geometry/table cases.
Pending split, retry and completion ignore unused new profile/timing input without mutating the base event.
Keep existing profile-free DCS1 rejection and TCS1-4/DCS2 fixtures passing.
Then test real hydraulic mass, accepted-only publication, decoded restart, invalid-input preflight and internally progressed rollback at O0/O2 with exact transcript identity.
non_goals: Automatic crop/root geometry, TCS1 daily-stress accumulation, alternate state owner, numerical acceptance changes, calendar/parser, surface delivery or canonical admission.
